comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment: Please paint a dedicated left turn lane on South Quarry Ridge Dr, turning left to E Horseman park dr. They painted a center lane, and traffic is always uncertain of which lane they should make the left turn from. It's rather dangerous situation and has a lot of foot traffic from the pickle ball courts and schools.

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
Dear mayor and city council members,

I understand a city council position is open. I would like to put Jami Leavitt's name at the top of the list. She had the next highest votes from the previous election so that tells me the voters have spoken. I met her only once but felt she was open, approachable, and reasonable.

I think she deserves the appointment, and would make an excellent council member for all of us.

Deanna Howard

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
Dear mayor and city council members,

You will soon be casting your vote to replace the seat Jimmie vacates as he becomes mayor. I had the pleasure of meeting Jami Leavitt this past fall, and was impressed by her openness, positive and friendly attitude, intelligence, grasp of the major challenges, and her willingness to engage, listen and build consensus. As the new mayor welcomes more constituent conversation with the city council, these traits will be very valuable. She also was the next highest in votes received in the last election, which I interpret as the constituents' choice. I think she deserves the appointment, and would make an excellent council member and teammate for you.

Tom Butine
St George

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
To St. George City Coucil Members:

I reside in The Cliffs of Snow Canuon. I had the opportunity to meet Jamie Leavitt this fall and I was impressed with her platform ideas, her openness to solutions and her knowledge of the issues facing St. George. Her professionalism and concern about creating and maintaining a high quality of life is apparent. I strongly indorse her to fill the vacant city council position.

Thank you for your time and consideration,
Patti Cleavinger

New York City made the decision to preserve Central Park. New York would not be the place it is without the efforts made by the leaders at the time.

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
I have a question of great import: What is the air velocity of an unladen swallow?

Sorry—I couldn't resist. What my actual comment/question relates to is Navajo Drive in Bloomington, where it connects with Apex Mine Road leading into the Bearclaw Poppy area. I lived on that road for a short time near the entrance to BLM land, and I also have a sister who lives there and whom I visit at least once a month.

My concern is with people—whether in cars, ATVs, dirt bikes, or other vehicles—who speed in and out of the entrance. It's certainly not everyone, but I've seen it happen often enough that it makes me nervous when approaching that part of the road.

Is there anything that can be done to encourage people to slow down and stop speeding as they enter and exit BLM land?

My inner-Karen has wondered if a speed bump or some other traffic-calming measure could be set up on the city side heading into BLM land

notes: All 6 comments are forwarded JotForm submissions. Page 2 is the map image attachment (IMG_0743.jpeg) belonging to Todd London's comment on page 1.
